To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TCR–HLA–peptide interface can undergo a conformational change in response to changes in the length of the peptide antigen.

the MEL5 MHC‐restricted TCR undergoes a structural change to accommodate a peptide that is presented by its cognate MHC molecule in a distinct conformation, thus altering the peptide's MHC anchor residue.
the T‐cell receptor (TCR) can induce a conformational change in the peptide antigen to accommodate a different anchor residue, which is important for future therapeutic strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how T‐cell receptors (TCRs) recognize and discriminate among foreign and self‐derived peptide antigens presented by major histocompatibility complex (MHC) proteins.
the molecular mechanisms that underpin the interaction between antigen‐specific T cells and their targets, with the goal of improving the design of immunotherapies.
the molecular basis for antigen recognition by T lymphocytes, which are key players in the human immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the T‐cell receptor (TCR) is a flexible molecule, capable of adapting to the antigenic ligand, which is presented by the Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) molecule, to achieve a stable TCR–peptid-MHC interaction.
TCR‐induced alterations in MHC anchor residue can be observed in the MEL5/HLA‐A2/AAGIGILTV TCR complex.
the nonapeptide and decapeptide are not equivalent epitopes, and that the nonapepide is a better epitope than the decapeptide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TCR‐induced conformational changes in the MHC‐peptide complex can lead to altered peptide anchor residue.
the TCR‐mediated induced‐fit mechanism of antigen recognition is a key factor in T cell activation.
the TCR‐induced alteration in primary MHC anchor residue is a mechanism by which T cells recognize their peptide antigen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TCR can induce conformational changes in the MHC–peptide complex, which can lead to altered antigen recognition and thus, potentially, T‐cell dysfunction.
there are many ways in which T cells can alter their peptide‐MHC recognition.
the MEL5 structure is a paradigm of the flexibility of TCR‐pMHC complexes and how this flexibility may be used to accommodate a variety of peptides and MHC molecules.
